profile.campus: Google Central Ohio (New Albany / Columbus-Lockbourne / Lancaster), OH
profile.address: Babbitt Road, New Albany, Plain Township, Franklin County, OH 43004 (2)
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's New Albany, Ohio data center campus, mapped on Babbitt Road in Plain Township, Franklin County, and carries the informational label NBY-5 in this registry's underlying mapping data, not independently confirmed against a Google-published building index this session. Google's own Ohio locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within the campus.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Ohio data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company broke ground in New Albany in 2019 and has since invested more than $20 billion in the state across New Albany, Lancaster, and Columbus, generating $21.7 billion in Ohio economic activity in 2025 and contributing over $16 million in philanthropic giving since 2006.

New Albany has become the anchor of Ohio's central data center corridor since Google broke ground there in 2019, alongside major campuses for Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services, all separately tracked in this registry, though Google's own public materials describe its New Albany footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings, addresses, or per-building capacity figures.

American Electric Power (AEP Ohio) is the principal electric utility serving most of the New Albany and Columbus-area data center market, and has filed with Ohio regulators for new large-load electric tariff structures in response to rapidly growing data center demand in the corridor. New Albany's community authority has used tax-increment financing agreements, and Ohio's state-level data center sales and use tax abatement program, to help anchor the cluster's continued growth alongside Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Google does not publish megawatt capacity, square footage, or building-level specifications for NBY-5. The facility is part of a multi-county campus in the New Albany and Columbus corridor where Google has disclosed a combined $1.7 billion investment across new data center projects, placing it alongside AWS and Meta as a major hyperscale operator in the same regional cluster.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, but only 8 publish power capacity figures, totaling 60.4 MW. Google's published capacity in the state ranks ninth by that total. The absence of published figures for NBY-5 means its scale relative to other Ohio facilities cannot be read from the operator's disclosures.

The binding constraint on assessing NBY-5's importance to AI scaling is the lack of published power or footprint data. Without capacity figures, the site's contribution to grid load, rack density, or regional compute availability cannot be quantified. Google's investment scale in the region signals hyperscale intent, but individual facility specifications remain opaque.
